messages:
ashley: :warning: FYI — GPU sync jobs are failing between pods in different namespaces (gpu-tenantA -> gpu-tenantB). Started after we tightened default network policies earlier today. Seeing packet loss and timeouts during shard sync. Anyone seen this pattern?

miguel: which pods/nodes? is this overlay CNI or azure-vnet? also paste `kubectl get networkpolicy -n gpu-tenantb` output and `kubectl get pods -o wide` please.

ashley: pods are gpu-sync-0 (ns gpu-tenantA) -> gpu-sync-2 (ns gpu-tenantB). Nodes: aks-gpupool-01/02 in different nodepool-subnets. We use Azure CNI (vnet-native). Quick outputs: 

```
kubectl get networkpolicy -n gpu-tenantb
NAME                 POD-SELECTOR   POLICY-TYPES
deny-egress-default  app=gpu-sync    Egress
\n# deny-egress-default rule (yaml snippet)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gpu-sync
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.128.0/24
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 443
```

Also ran `ip a` on node; node podCIDR looks like 10.2.0.0/16 for nodes in gpupool-02 and 10.1.0.0/16 in gpupool-01.

linh: sounds like the policy only allows egress to a single /24 (maybe from an older nodepool). Azure CNI gives pods VNET IPs; different nodepools use different subnets. If NP only whitelists 10.1.128.0/24, pods on 10.2.x won't be reachable.

devon: also check MTU/encapsulation — we saw fragmentation issues earlier when nodepools were on different AZs with different upstream switches. tcpdump might show "ICMP Fragmentation Needed" on sync flows. RDMA won't work across overlay either, but here it looks like pure IP block mismatch.

ashley: ran tcpdump briefly, saw a bunch of retransmits and one ICMP line: 
```
15:34:12.123456 IP 10.1.12.7 > 10.2.5.9: UDP, length 1420
15:34:12.123789 IP 10.2.5.9 > 10.1.12.7: ICMP 3/4, Fragmentation needed and DF set
```

miguel: yep fragmentation + wrong cidr in NP. Quick mitigation: update deny-egress-default to include the other pod CIDRs (10.2.0.0/16) or switch to namespaceSelector/podSelector-based allow where possible. For immediate recovery, allow egress to podCIDR ranges for cluster.

ashley: applied a scoped patch to the NP to include both pod CIDRs and the overlay ranges. Patch: 
```
# egress additions (applied)
- to:
  - ipBlock:
      cidr: 10.1.0.0/16
  - ipBlock:
      cidr: 10.2.0.0/16
```

After patch: GPU sync success, no more retransmits. :white_check_mark:

devon: great. Follow-ups: 
- audit other tenant NPs for hardcoded /24s (likely from old nodepool)
- add an infra runbook entry for "NPs must include cluster podCIDRs or use podSelector/namespaceSelector"
- add CI/netpolicy lint check to infra repo (detect ipBlock references that don't match cluster config)

ashley: filing a short playbook and PR for NP linting. Will also tag networking on the PR. Thanks all.

miguel: also add a note to nodepool provisioning docs: when creating new nodepools in new subnet ranges, communicate podCIDR to security team so NP templates can be updated.

linh: I'll follow up with a quick script to dump all NPs that reference ipBlock and cross-check against current cluster podCIDRs.

ashley: awesome — saved us from a long outage. Closing this thread once the PR lands.
